cls: Next-generation ROS1 and pan-TRK inhibitor (macrocyclic tyrosine kinase inhibitor)
pharm: Macrocyclic tyrosine kinase inhibitor of ROS1 and tropomyosin receptor kinases TRKA, TRKB, and TRKC, including common resistance mutations; used in ROS1-positive NSCLC and NTRK fusion-positive solid tumors
quick: 160 mg orally once daily for 14 days, then 160 mg twice daily
Take with or without food at about the same times each day
Can cause fetal harm; non-hormonal contraception during and for months after last dose
Do not breastfeed during and for 10 days after the last dose
No adjustment in mild-moderate; severe/ESRD not studied
No adjustment in mild; moderate-severe not studied; monitor LFTs
No specific interaction; limit due to additive CNS effects
CNS symptoms, pulmonary symptoms (ILD), LFTs, CPK, uric acid, pregnancy status
summary: Repotrectinib (Augtyro) is a next-generation macrocyclic tyrosine kinase inhibitor of ROS1 and TRKA/B/C, active against common resistance mutations. It is indicated for adults with locally advanced or metastatic ROS1-positive NSCLC and for adults and children 12 years and older with NTRK fusion-positive solid tumors after prior therapy or with no satisfactory alternative. Dosing is 160 mg orally once daily for 14 days, then 160 mg twice daily until progression or unacceptable toxicity, with or without food. Most patients develop CNS effects (dizziness, ataxia, cognitive changes); other serious risks are ILD/pneumonitis, hepatotoxicity, myalgia with CPK elevation, hyperuricemia, skeletal fractures, and embryo-fetal toxicity. It is a CYP3A substrate and inducer: avoid strong/moderate CYP3A inhibitors, inducers, and P-gp inhibitors, and use non-hormonal contraception.
indications: Locally advanced or metastatic ROS1-positive non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) in adults

Locally advanced, unresectable, or metastatic solid tumors with an NTRK gene fusion in adults and pediatric patients 12 years and older who have progressed after prior therapy or have no satisfactory alternative therapy

dosage.c: ROS1-positive NSCLC and NTRK fusion-positive solid tumors
dosage.d: 160 mg orally once daily for 14 days, then 160 mg orally twice daily; continue until disease progression or unacceptable toxicity
dosage.n: With or without food; for adults and pediatric patients 12 years and older per labeling
dosage.r: Adult and pediatric 12 years and older, oral
dosage.t: Once daily x14 days, then twice daily

dosage.d: First reduction 120 mg twice daily; second reduction 80 mg twice daily; permanently discontinue if 80 mg twice daily is not tolerated
dosage.n: Withhold for CNS effects, ILD/pneumonitis, hepatotoxicity, CPK elevation, hyperuricemia, or fractures per severity tables in labeling

dosage.c: Concomitant CYP3A or P-gp interacting drugs
dosage.d: Avoid strong and moderate CYP3A inhibitors, strong and moderate CYP3A inducers, and P-gp inhibitors during treatment
dosage.n: Stop CYP3A inhibitors for 3 to 5 half-lives of the inhibitor before starting repotrectinib

admin: Swallow capsules whole with or without food at about the same times each day; do not open, crush, or chew
Follow the lead-in strictly: once daily for the first 14 days, then twice daily thereafter
If a dose is missed or vomiting occurs after a dose, skip it and take the next dose at the regularly scheduled time; do not take two doses together
Discontinue strong and moderate CYP3A inhibitors for 3 to 5 half-lives of the inhibitor before starting therapy
Assess neurologic status, pulmonary symptoms, liver tests, CPK, and uric acid as scheduled during treatment
moa: Repotrectinib is a macrocyclic tyrosine kinase inhibitor of ROS1 and the tropomyosin receptor kinases TRKA, TRKB, and TRKC, including common acquired resistance (solvent-front) mutations. By occupying the kinase ATP pocket it blocks ROS1- and TRK-driven downstream signaling for proliferation and survival in ROS1-rearranged NSCLC and NTRK fusion-positive tumors. It distributes into the central nervous system, which contributes to both intracranial activity and CNS adverse effects.

absolute: Known serious hypersensitivity to repotrectinib or any component
monitor: Neurologic status (dizziness, ataxia, cognition, mood, sleep)
Liver tests, CPK, and uric acid during treatment
Signs of skeletal fracture (pain, mobility change, deformity)
relative: Preexisting CNS disorders (dizziness, ataxia, cognitive impairment risk)
Concomitant strong or moderate CYP3A inhibitors, inducers, or P-gp inhibitors

preg: Based on its mechanism and animal findings, repotrectinib can cause fetal harm. Verify pregnancy status before starting. Advise females of reproductive potential to use effective non-hormonal contraception during treatment and for 2 months after the last dose, and advise males with female partners of reproductive potential to use effective contraception during treatment and for 4 months after the last dose.
lact: There are no data on repotrectinib in human milk or its effects on the breastfed child or milk production. Because of the potential for serious adverse reactions, advise women not to breastfeed during treatment and for 10 days after the last dose.
renal: No dose adjustment is recommended for mild or moderate renal impairment. Repotrectinib has not been adequately studied in severe renal impairment or end-stage renal disease; use with caution and monitor closely.
hepatic: No dose adjustment is recommended for mild hepatic impairment. Repotrectinib has not been adequately studied in moderate or severe hepatic impairment; monitor liver tests closely. Monitor ALT, AST, and bilirubin every 2 weeks during the first month, then monthly and as clinically indicated.

interactions.alcohol: No specific interaction is described; avoid or limit alcohol because of additive CNS effects (dizziness, ataxia, cognitive impairment).
interactions.diagnostics: Monitor liver tests (ALT, AST, bilirubin) every 2 weeks in the first month then monthly; check CPK with muscle symptoms and uric acid before and periodically during treatment.
interactions.food: Take with or without food at about the same times each day; no clinically meaningful food effect.
major: Strong and moderate CYP3A inhibitors (raise repotrectinib exposure; avoid)
Strong and moderate CYP3A inducers (lower repotrectinib exposure; avoid)
Hormonal contraceptives (reduced efficacy from CYP3A induction; use effective non-hormonal methods)
CYP3A substrates where minimal concentration changes reduce efficacy (avoid concomitant use)
minor: Acid-reducing agents have no described clinically meaningful effect on repotrectinib exposure.
moderate: CNS depressants (additive dizziness, ataxia, cognitive and sleep effects)

emergency: New or worsening cough, dyspnea, or fever (possible ILD/pneumonitis) - seek urgent care
Severe dizziness, ataxia, confusion, or fainting
Severe muscle pain or weakness, especially with dark urine
New severe bone pain or deformity (possible fracture)
rare: Fractures at sites of prior disease or radiation
serious: Central nervous system effects (dizziness, ataxia, cognitive impairment)

monitoring: Neurologic review (dizziness, ataxia, cognition, mood, sleep) with dose hold or reduction per severity
Pulmonary symptoms; withhold immediately for suspected ILD/pneumonitis and discontinue permanently if confirmed
Liver tests every 2 weeks in the first month, then monthly and as indicated
Serum CPK with unexplained muscle pain, tenderness, or weakness; serum uric acid before and periodically during treatment
Pregnancy verification before starting; fracture symptoms (pain, mobility change, deformity)
counsel: Take once daily for the first 14 days, then twice daily, with or without food at about the same times each day; swallow capsules whole
If you miss a dose or vomit after a dose, skip it and take the next dose on time; never double up
Dizziness, balance problems, confusion, or memory changes are common; do not drive or operate machinery if affected and tell your team promptly
Report new or worsening cough, shortness of breath, or fever (lung inflammation), muscle pain or weakness, gout-like joint pain, or any new bone pain
Use effective non-hormonal birth control during treatment and as directed after stopping; do not breastfeed during treatment
pk: Antitumor responses develop over weeks; CNS effects often begin within the first 1 to 2 weeks
Peak plasma concentrations occur within a few hours of oral dosing; steady state is reached during the 14-day once-daily lead-in
Mean terminal half-life about 61 hours after a single dose and about 40 hours at steady state
Continuous twice-daily dosing (after lead-in) until disease progression or unacceptable toxicity
Store at 20-25 C (68-77 F); excursions 15-30 C (59-86 F) permitted
pearls: The 14-day once-daily lead-in precedes twice-daily dosing; do not start twice daily early
CNS effects affect most patients (dizziness, ataxia, cognitive changes) and usually appear in the first weeks; hold and reduce per labeling rather than pushing through
ILD/pneumonitis: withhold for any suspicion and discontinue permanently if confirmed
Hormonal contraception is unreliable (CYP3A induction); non-hormonal methods are required
Fractures can occur with minimal or no trauma; evaluate new bone pain promptly
missed: If a dose of repotrectinib is missed, or if vomiting occurs at any time after taking a dose, skip that dose and take the next dose at the regularly scheduled time. Do not take two doses together to make up for a missed or vomited dose.
overdose: There is no specific antidote for repotrectinib overdose. Manage with supportive care and monitor for CNS, pulmonary, hepatic, muscle, and metabolic toxicity, including ECG, liver tests, CPK, and uric acid. Contact Poison Help (1-800-222-1222).
